query: How would HelpfulnessNumerator change if reviews provided more detailed product information?

per_column.name: ProductInfoCompletenessScore
per_column.rationale: A continuous measure of how much detailed product information a review provides. This is exactly the lever named in the query ('more detailed product information') and is intervenable, since a reviewer could choose to include more detail.

per_column.name: HasDetailedProductInfo
per_column.rationale: A binary indicator of whether the review contains detailed product info; an alternative operationalization of the same treatment named in the query. Intervenable (a reviewer can decide to add detail), but redundant with the score column and still just the treatment.

judge.rationale: The added columns capture only the treatment (detail/completeness of product information), which is exactly what the query names, and provide it in two redundant forms (continuous score and binary flag). No confounders are supplied at all. A valid what-if analysis of the effect of information detail on HelpfulnessNumerator requires adjusting for common causes of both the treatment and the outcome that are NOT named in the query -- e.g., review length/verbosity, product category or popularity, reviewer expertise/engagement, star Score, or how long the review has been visible (Time / exposure, which also drives HelpfulnessDenominator). None of these were added. Because the operator only re-expressed the treatment and named zero confounders, it fails the decisive test: it does not surface any un-named common causes needed to identify the counterfactual effect. Confounder capability under test is not demonstrated.
